messages:
Aisha: ping — Acme SRE reporting a reproducible issue: when they call our tool endpoint they sometimes get the output from a completely different tool. Started after last night's registry migration.
Aisha: repro attached by customer (sanitized):\n```
POST /v1/tools/call HTTP/1.1\nHost: api.redwood.ai\nAuthorization: Bearer xxxxx\nContent-Type: application/json\n{\n  \"tool_handle\": \"TranslateText\",\n  \"args\": { \"text\": \"Bonjour\", \"to\": \"en\" }\n}
```
Aisha: response body they saw: `{"result":"Processed by SummarizeV1","output":"short summary..."}` — clearly wrong tool output + 200. They show request-id header: `req_2026_04_02_88a3` and trace id `trace-9c7`.
Ben: can you paste the raw response headers and the exact tool_handle string the client sent? need to check if it's case or unicode normalization. :mag:
Aisha: headers: `x-request-id: req_2026_04_02_88a3`, `x-trace-id: trace-9c7`, `x-gateway-node: gw-14`. client used capitalized "TranslateText" (T caps, camelCase). Customer insists they never changed their code.
Jordan: initial hypothesis: registry backfill/migration introduced alias mapping churn — if the registry's lookup is doing strict case-sensitive match, but the runtime store normalized handles to kebab-case or snake_case, that could map to wrong UUIDs. Another possibility: a short-lived index swap during manifest rollout caused handle->uuid pointers to be briefly inconsistent between gateway and runtime.
registry-bot: manifest rollout completed at 2026-04-02T03:12Z (deploy id: mf-331). Affected shards: registry-1, registry-2. TTLs for client caches = 60s.
Ben: can we find the mapping for the uuid returned in the response? Aisha can we get the gateway logs for gw-14 around the request time? grep for req_2026_04_02_88a3.
Aisha: pasted log excerpt: `2026-04-02T03:21:14Z gw-14 req=req_2026_04_02_88a3 lookup: handle="TranslateText" -> uuid=uuid-77b mapped-to service=SummarizeV1 (via alias translate-text-v1)`. Full trace shows gateway did a registry lookup and resolved to SummarizeV1.
Ben: ok that confirms the gateway resolved the handle to wrong uuid. Likely two aliases collided during migration. Jordan, can you run quick query against registry to show current handle records? e.g.:
```
SELECT handle, canonical_handle, uuid FROM tool_handles WHERE handle ILIKE '%translat%';
```
Jordan: ran query, results: `TranslateText` -> canonical `translate-text` -> uuid=uuid-77b (old mapping), `translate_text` -> canonical `translate_text` -> uuid=uuid-a12 (the new translator). There are two entries because the migration created snake_case aliases for some handles and didn't remove the older alias entries.
Ben: aha. So gateway's lookup prefers exact-string matches without normalization and returns the first matching alias. Customer sending `TranslateText` hits the old alias that points to SummarizeV1. We should avoid changing alias semantics mid-rollout.
Aisha: customer wants immediate mitigation — they can't rollout changes on their side. Any quick fixes to restore correct mapping for them?
Jordan: two options: 1) flush the gateway cache for this customer so it re-queries the authoritative registry (but registry currently contains both aliases so might still pick wrong one), 2) create an explicit alias mapping for `TranslateText` -> uuid-a12 (manual override) scoped to Acme account, or 3) enable casefold normalization in gateway lookup so camelCase/kebab/snake map consistently (requires canary deploy). For hotfix I'd do #2 scoped to their org.
Ben: agree. I'll add an org-scoped alias override. Command: `registryctl alias add --org acme --handle TranslateText --uuid uuid-a12 --reason "hotfix: post-migration collision"` — will also add audit tag and TTL 72h.
Aisha: pls proceed. Customer asked for rollback if we see more collisions.
Ben: done — alias override inserted (audit id adv-449). I also added a short watch on gw-14 and logged hits for handle TranslateText. :white_check_mark:
Aisha: customer confirmed within 3m that calls now return translator output. They also asked for root cause breakdown and a postmortem.
Jordan: I'll open a short postmortem. Action items: revert duplicate alias creation in the migration script, add a uniqueness constraint on (lower(handle), org) in registry DB, and add a canary step to validate handle->uuid mappings before switching manifests. I'll own the DB change.
Ben: I'll draft the rollback plan and a small gateway change to do fallback matching by lowercasing handles if exact fails. Canary it in eng-staging first.
Aisha: adding follow-up ticket for customer comms and billing check (no failed charges but double-check logs). Thanks everyone. :heart:
Jordan: filing PMR and linking to this thread. tagging ops to monitor for similar collisions. :clipboard:
